nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
# IMAGE – MiniMax H3
Reference images (optional) + an instruction in plain words in, one image out: start and end frames, style frames, the same place from a new angle.

1. **Models** (group 1): download links are in the notes on the left.
2. **Settings** (group 3): **NAME** = output folder · **RESOLUTION**: aspect ratio + scale (1.5x = 2016×1152 for the frame, 1.0x = a fast 4-step test) · **Seed** = a new variant · **TURBO?** on = 8 fast steps, off = the official 50 steps (~3× slower).
3. **Prompt** (4a): what you want in the green **INSTRUCTION** box, in normal sentences. **STYLE** and **WORLD** once for every image. Copy a start from the *Instruction presets* note.
4. **REF IMAGE 1–4** (4b): characters, cars, a place, an earlier frame. Bypass the ones you don't need (**Ctrl+B**); all bypassed = from the prompt alone.
5. Run.

**Switches** (group 3)
* **UPSCALE?** (7): H3 re-draws the image at 4032×2304 with the same prompt and references; **BEFORE / AFTER UPSCALE** compares both.

**Output:** `output/AnimeH3/Image/NAME/`: `NAME_00001.png` (workflow embedded), with the upscale `NAME_2x_00001.png`. Format (png / avif / exr): on the result node. Same 1.75:1 shape as the videos, so a start frame drops straight into the Video workflow.

**Watch out**
* `<Picture N>` counts the active REF IMAGEs in order: bypassing one renumbers the rest.
* A full-frame photo of a place makes H3 copy its camera: use one only for big camera changes (reverse angle, bird's-eye view).

**Needs** ComfyUI 0.37.0 or newer + [KJNodes](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes), [Mickmumpitz Nodes](https://github.com/mickmumpitz/ComfyUI-Mickmumpitz-Nodes), [rgthree](https://github.com/rgthree/rgthree-comfy), [MMH3 Ultimate Upscale](https://github.com/bbaudio-2025/Comfyui-MMH3-UltimateUpscale). Red nodes: *Missing Node Packs* → **Install All** → restart.

nodes.title: STYLE
widgets_values: 2D anime screencap, flat cel-shaded illustration, hand-drawn manga-style ink line art. Late-1990s Japanese street-racing anime style, dramatic high-contrast look, with a retro, slightly rough hand-inked feel: heavier black ink contour weight, faint pen-line wobble as if inked by hand frame by frame, a light halftone-dot shading pattern layered into the darkest shadow shapes, subtle scan-line grain across the frame, warm slightly desaturated retro color grading. Flat solid color fills with strong, clearly separated cel-shading — one hard-edged core shadow tone and a brighter secondary highlight tone per surface. A clean picture: the frame shows only the scene.

nodes.title: WORLD
widgets_values: The street on the outskirts of Shibuwaka, a small town in rural Japan, at clear midday: small shops with plain flat color signboards, a row of brightly colored drink vending machines, trimmed hedges, pastel apartment blocks with laundry-hung balconies, and utility poles with dense black cables sagging across a flat hazy pale sky. Daylight falls as hard-edged flat shadow shapes, with crisp flat highlights on painted metal and glass.

nodes.title: Instruction presets
widgets_values:
## Instruction presets – copy into INSTRUCTION, change the CAPS

**Start frame**
```
<Picture 1> is CHARACTER / CAR, <Picture 2> is CHARACTER / CAR. Start frame: WHO is WHERE, doing WHAT, seen from CAMERA POSITION, WHO on the LEFT, WHO on the RIGHT.
```

**End frame** – continues a start frame
```
<Picture 1> is the start frame of a shot. End frame of the same shot, WHAT HAS CHANGED (e.g. the green car has passed the blue car and is now ahead). Same place, same camera position, same light.
```

**Style frame** – look and mood
```
<Picture 1> is CHARACTER / CAR. Style frame: a dramatic key image of SCENE, LIGHT AND MOOD (e.g. low evening sun, long shadows, glowing tail lights).
```

**Same place, new angle** – make it a big change; a small one comes out as a copy
```
<Picture 1> shows a place, photographed from another camera position; this image takes a new camera: NEW CAMERA POSITION. Show exactly the same place with the same buildings, signs and street furniture (e.g. "reverse angle: the camera is turned around by 180 degrees and now stands at …", or "a steep bird's-eye view from high above").
```

**Edit**
```
<Picture 1> is the image to edit. Keep everything exactly as it is, only CHANGE (e.g. it is night now, wet street, lit shop signs).
```

**Clay render / photo → anime frame**
```
<Picture 1> is a grey 3D layout render / a photo. Redraw exactly this composition, camera and layout as a finished anime frame: WHAT THE GREY SHAPES ARE.
```

**Places:** one WORLD block per location (buildings, signs, street furniture, light), reused in every image there.

nodes.title: PROMPT TEMPLATE · with references
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
The reference pictures are <Picture 1> and every picture after it. The instruction says what each one shows and how it is used.

summary:
[reference generation] The target is one completely still frame. {INSTRUCTION}

retention_analysis:
Every character, vehicle, object and place taken from a reference picture keeps its exact design, colours and details, except where the instruction says otherwise. The camera position, framing and composition come from the instruction; a reference keeps its own camera only where the instruction says so.
